newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's supreme court set to resume telcom ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's supreme court set to resume telcom ruling.

text.p: Brazil's supreme court Thursday was likely to resume study of a request for an injunction that would suspend the government's program to privatize cellular telephone services, a court spokesman said.
"It's probably going to be today but there are two other cases to be heard first. If they take up a lot of time the telecommunications case could be delayed," said spokesman Irineu Tamanini.

The Supreme Federal Tribunal began studying in February the constitutionality of a so-called Minimum Law which the government introduced in 1996 as a legal framework for its plan to tender out concessions to run B Band cellular services.
The case, brought by left-wing political parties opposed to the government's privatization program, was put on hold for ten working days to receive more information on the law.
A court ruling in favor of the opposition would put on hold the government's plan to begin the B Band concession program April 7, when bids from would-be operators are due in.
